Top of the Morning
 

Illustration: Allie Carl/Axios
 

Cleaning out the notebook as we kick off the first full week of Q4...

🔨 Regulatory revelation: The SEC last week called for increased rigor when it comes to private asset valuations, with a particular focus on private credit.

  • Consider this something of a regulatory compass, showing where the SEC is paying closest attention.
  • Most notable, the SEC reminded private credit managers that they are required to make fair value measurements on a timely basis — with macro events to be considered — even if not contractually obligated to provide reports in the same time frame to investors.
  • It also emphasized that valuation techniques and inputs must be clearly disclosed, adding that "boilerplate" language may not be sufficient.

💼 VC-land: Notable Capital is out raising its 10th fund, but without managing partner Jeff Richards on the Form D. Fellow managing partners Glenn Solomon and Hans Tung are listed.

  • Richards declined to discuss fundraising, natch, but tells me via text: "I remain 100% active and engaged; just decided not to make new investments from the next fund. It gives our younger investors like Dan [Cahana] and Chelcie [Taylor] room to run ... I currently sit on 14 boards, five of which are >$100m ARR, so quite busy ... It's an incredible time to be in venture in Silicon Valley."
  • Notable is the U.S. venture group that once was known as GGV Capital, before splitting with its China arm due to geopolitical tensions.

💰 More VC-land: Chad Byers is raising a new eponymous venture fund, per an SEC filing, but tells me that he isn't leaving Susa Ventures — which he co-founded. He declined to comment further.

  • Byers Capital Group 1 lists the same office address as Susa, but doesn't list its other general partners.

🎵 Coming attractions: Don't be surprised to see Shamrock Capital in market soon with its second debt opportunities fund.

  • The LA-based firm, which focuses on media and entertainment deals, is said to have fully deployed its debut $191 million debt fund — quietly closing 10 loans, only two of which have been publicly announced (Welsh soccer club Swansea City and Roblox game developer Voldex).
  • It can recycle via that fund's realizations, and has dry powder for equity investments out of its flagship and content funds, but there's growing demand in areas like music and sports for asset-backed loans — particularly among content owners who don't want to dilute their ownership stakes.

🤖 Robotic rupture: There's a disagreement among venture capitalists when it comes to funding physical AI, which was explored a bit last week during my on-stage interview with Bain Capital Ventures partner Ajay Agarwal.

  • Some are plugging big money into robot "brain" developers, believing that the trained models can be plugged into a variety of different hardware. The physics, they argue, remain constant, and hardware is often where venture dollars go to die.
  • Agarwal is on the other side, perhaps based on his experience backing Kiva Systems — which was acquired by Amazon and became the foundation for its warehouse robotics system. He believes that the winners will be full-stack, due to the need for sector specialization.

✨ SV-to-DC: Andreessen Horowitz spurred a lot of Silicon Valley's shift toward Republicans in the 2024 elections, and now has one of its top alumni on President Trump's new AI task force (I'm sorry, his new "Super Intelligence Force").

  • Scott Kupor was one of a16z's first employees, spending 16 years as managing partner before leaving to join Trump 2.0 as head of the Office of Personnel Management (a role he'll keep).
  • The group is being chaired by DNI Jay Clayton, and also includes FTC chair Andrew Ferguson and Uber vet and current Pentagon CTO Emil Michael.
 
 
The BFD
 

Illustration: Sarah Grillo/Axios
 

Schneider Electric (Paris: SU) has agreed to buy Boston-based industrial software maker PTC (Nasdaq: PTC) for $22.6 billion.

Why it's the BFD: Software mega-mergers are rare in 2026, as sector dealmaking has been trapped by AI-powered uncertainty.

By the numbers: Schneider will pay $205 per share, representing a 42.3% premium to Friday's closing price.

The bottom line: PTC would be Schneider's largest-ever acquisition, topping its $11 billion purchase of Aveva in 2023, and its third billion-dollar-plus deal this year.
 
 
Venture Capital Deals
 

• Valon Technologies, an NYC-based OS for regulated finance, raised $150m in Series D funding at a $2.3b post-money valuation. Ribbit Capital led, joined by insiders like a16z. axios.link/4hIU4IM

• Quartermaster, an Arlington, Va.-based maritime intelligence startup, raised $100m in Series B equity funding. Insight Partners led, joined by Overmatch Ventures, First Round Capital, Quiet Capital, Steel Atlas, and TMV. It also secured $40m in venture debt. axios.link/4y77xjN

• Namespace, an SF-based developer infrastructure platform, raised $42m in Series B funding, per Axios Pro. Scale Venture Partners led, joined by 20VC, NEA, Essence, and Burst Capital. axios.link/4yxMFDi

• OneByZero, a Singaporean enterprise AI startup, raised $20m in Series A funding led by Jungle Ventures. axios.link/4dp7vMC

• Buntar Aerospace, a Ukrainian maker of reconnaissance drones, raised $16m. The Freedom Fund led, joined by Gardar, Iron Wolf, and Autonomy Capital. axios.link/3TKRkSW

• Pandektes, a legal research tech startup, raised €13.5m in Series A funding. Alstin Capital led, joined by PROfounders and Scale Capital. axios.link/471mLM4

• SafeWorld, a Palo Alto, Calif.-based developer of robot safety simulation technologies, raised $12.2m in seed funding. Shine Capital and a16z Speedrun led, joined by Box Group, Carnegie Mellon University Endowment, Innovation Endeavors, and SV Angel. axios.link/4hFKc2p

• Fleuret AI, a French penetration testing startup, raised €4m in pre-seed funding. Raise Ventures led, joined by Auriga Cyber Ventures, Wind, and Better Angle. axios.link/47zRZKl

Private Equity Deals
 

• Axis Capital is weighing a bid for Permanent TSB, an Irish retail lender whose shareholders approved a €1.6b takeover offer from Austria's BAWAG ⁠Group. axios.link/47y03v3

• Blackstone, KKR and Warburg Pincus are weighing bids for windshield repair company Cary, which is owned by CVC Capital Partners and Nordic Capital, per Bloomberg. axios.link/3VvDLaD

• Graycliff Partners invested in ValveTek Utility Services and MeterTek Utility Services, Kenilworth, N.J.-based providers of water meter and distribution system services to water utilities. axios.link/3W6KesM

• Growth Capital Partners invested in Agilia, a London-based infrastructure consultancy. axios.link/4yvLJ1X

• Intertape Polymer Group, a Clearlake portfolio company, acquired Clysar, a Clinton, Iowa-based manufacturer of polyolefin shrink film. axios.link/4jJucie

• OceanSound Partners invested in IMSAR, a Springville, Utah-based maker of synthetic aperture radar payloads and mission software. axios.link/4xYuGob

⚡ TDR Capital agreed to buy OCU Group, a U.K. energy transformation and infrastructure services platform, from Triton Partners. axios.link/4ycRbpS

• Trustly, a Swedish digital payments company, raised $40m from insiders Nordic Capital and Alfvén & Didrikson. axios.link/4htKb2I

• Warburg Pincus invested in Awayday, a Destin, Fla.-based vacation rental management company controlled by Ares Private Equity and LightBay Capital. axios.link/3VvbvF8
 
 
Public Offerings
 

No companies expect to price IPOs this week on U.S. exchanges.

• Mynt, a Philippine fintech, expects to be valued at around $7b in its domestic IPO. It's raised nearly $800m from firms like Ant Group, Insight Partners, and Warburg Pincus. axios.link/4rQ3QgL

🚑 TRex Bio, a South SF-based developer of precision immunoregulatory medicines, set IPO terms at 8.3m shares at $14-$16. It would have a $453m fully diluted value at the midpoint and plans to list on the Nasdaq (TRXB). TRex has raised over $220m from firms like Eli Lilly (which is buying back in via the IPO), Janus Henderson, Balyasny Asset Management, Affinity Asset Advisors, Alexandria Venture Investments, Avego BioScience Capital, Delos Capital, J&J Innovation, Pfizer Ventures, Polaris Partners, and SV Health Investors. axios.link/4rKpAdQ
 
 
Liquidity Events
 

🚑 Boyu Capital is weighing a sale of Quasar Medical, a Singaporean medical device CDMO, per Bloomberg. axios.link/4jaejkZ

• Firy (NYSE: FIRY) sold its entire 10.5% equity stake in Germany's Exit Games back to the company for $55m in cash. axios.link/4zctb6O

🚑 GE HealthCare (Nasdaq: GEHC) agreed to buy Sofie Biosciences, a Dulles, Va.-based maker of cancer scan chemicals, for $945m in cash. Sofie backers include Trilantic. axios.link/46ZYh5W

🚑 Shionogi (Tokyo: 4507) agreed to buy IntraBio, an Austin, Texas-based rare disease biotech, for $2b. IntraBio had raised over $60m from firms like Biohealth Innovation. axios.link/4iYZ12h
 
 
More M&A
 

• AkzoNobel is in talks to sell its Southeast Asian decorative paints business to Nippon Paint (Tokyo: 4612) for over $1b, per the FT. axios.link/4ANh3uD

• BT Group (LSE: BT) will pay £400m to buy TalkTalk, a British low-cost internet service provider, out of administration. axios.link/4djLEWN

⚡ Cenovus Energy (TSX: CVE) agreed to buy Athabasca Oil (TSX: ATH) for around C$5.7b in cash and stock. axios.link/4hIT7Qs

• C.H. Robinson (Nasdaq: CHRW) agreed to acquire RXO (NYSE: RXO), a Charlotte, N.C.-based provider of truck brokerage services, for $5.8b in cash and stock. axios.link/4ANNAkh

• Curaleaf (TSX: CURA) sweetened its takeover bid for rival Aurora Cannabis (TSX: ACB). axios.link/4dUTN49

⚡ Galp Energia, a listed Portuguese oil company, is exploring options for its renewable energy business, including a possible sale, per Bloomberg. axios.link/4yrqxu9

• Intesa Sanpaolo (Milan: ISP) sweetened its takeover bid for rival Italian lender Banca Monte dei Paschi di Siena (M: BMPS) to €31.4b. axios.link/4y400SJ

⚡ Ithaca Energy (LSE: ITH) agreed to buy a portfolio of offshore oil projects from Suncor Energy (TSX: SU) for up to $1.11b. axios.link/4hsatSV
 
 
Fundraising
 

⚡ Energy Capital Partners raised an $834m single-asset CV for Next Wave Energy Partners, the operator of an alkylation complex next to the Houston Ship Channel. axios.link/4rKDIng

• Hingham Growth Partners, a consumer-focused fund led by Ben O'Connor (ex-BAM Elevate) and Julianne Hummelberg (Summit Partners), is raising its debut fund, per an SEC filing.

• Linse Capital, the growth-stage firm led by Goldman Sachs vets Michael Linse and Bastiaan Janmaat, raised $150m for an early-stage fund. linsecapital.com

• Niobrara Capital Partners, a tech-focused PE firm whose partners include Mike Pompeo and PE vet Chip Schorr, raised $1.1b for its debut fund ($1.5b including co-investment vehicles). axios.link/4AT0lKI
